relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 missense variant: "a missense mutation in the NOD2 gene with an Arginine → Glutamine exchange at codon 334, confirming the definitive diagnosis of BS".
method_note: Hand extraction of a short case report (no tables). The one patient is unlabelled, so label 'patient' (rule 5). The variant is printed only as a protein change ('R334Q'; also 'Arginine → Glutamine exchange at codon 334'); no transcript or cDNA printed, so cdna null and protein field holds 'R334Q' as printed (not p. notation). Zygosity, inheritance and parental testing not stated. 'one of the most frequent mutations observed in BS' is not recorded as a pathogenicity classification. Ages: the boy was 13 at referral to dermatology, then had 4 months of treatment and a 16-month follow-up, so 13 is not his age at last evaluation; age at last evaluation and overall onset left not reported. Skin lesion onset at 3 years recorded on the rash feature row only, since onset of arthritis/uveitis is not given. Skin biopsy 'without evidence of necrobiosis or vasculitis' is recorded as excluded feature rows, but the composite checklist vasculitis item (large-vessel arteritis, aortitis or leukocytoclastic vasculitis) is left not reported (narrow finding on one biopsy). No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: Previous systemic therapies: methotrexate, etanercept, leflunomide, adalimumab and golimumab; systemic and topical steroids (poor response, rapid relapse); UVA-1 phototherapy (25 sessions, cumulative 890 J/cm² over 4 months) with complete clearance of skin lesions and no relapse at 16-month follow-up
